fields.corePath: A home tiffin kitchen owner lands on the home page and clicks Start free route. Step 1, she puts in her subscriber list — name, flat or house number, society or area, veg or non-veg, morning or evening. She can paste it straight out of Excel, or press Use sample list if she wants to try it before typing 60 rows. Step 2, she enters the kitchen address and the time the dabbas leave, and picks two-wheeler, cycle or auto. Step 3, she presses Build route and waits about four seconds. Step 4, the route comes up on the map with every stop numbered and the distance and the total time under it. Step 5, she presses Send to delivery boy, which opens WhatsApp with the numbered stop list already written out, and she forwards it. That is the whole job done. No account is needed for the first route. We only ask for an email if she wants to save the route and open it again tomorrow.
fields.knownGaps: The routing is greedy nearest-neighbour, not optimal. On my own list of 46 Pune subscribers it comes out about 8% longer than what I get by hand in Google Maps, and I print that sentence on the result page instead of hiding it. Above roughly 80 stops it gets slow, around 11 seconds, and there is no loading state for that yet — the button just sits there looking dead, which I know is bad. Map tiles are OpenStreetMap so a lot of the newer Kharadi and NIBM society names are missing; you can see the road but not the building name, so the delivery boy still needs the flat number. Saving a route asks for an email and that email goes into Supabase with no verification, anyone can type anything. Morning and evening routes are built separately and I have not handled a subscriber who takes both — right now she has to appear in both lists. PDF download works on desktop Chrome, on iPhone Safari it opens a blank tab about half the time. None of this sits on the core path: building a route and sending it to WhatsApp work every time.
